I like this framing a lot: agent improvement is harness improvement, not model improvement

The interesting interventions are often at the tool boundary:
- what context you pass
- when tools are provided
- how you recover from failure
- what gets measured afterward

That’s the loop we’re building around deepagents (the orchestration logic) + LangSmith (how you measure)

quotedTweet.text:
Beyond Prompts: Measuring and Optimizing LLM Tool-Agent Harnesses — new paper (arXiv, 4 Sep 2026; accepted EMNLP 2026). https://t.co/pKJEV3lx5R

Treats harness optimization around a fixed model as budgeted selection: edits are guarded intercepts at the tool boundary, not rewrites of execution logic. PRISM clusters failures, routes each repair to a prompt, middleware, or joint surface, and picks candidates by gate pass-rate AND reliability (RelLift95), not score alone.

3 distinct takeaways for product builders:
- Report selected-harness reliability, not just mean lift. BH found the best individual harnesses but had negative reliable lift on both tau-bench domains — a strong explorer, an unreliable selector.
- Constrain middleware to tool-boundary edit patterns (silent correction, error blocking, prerequisite blocking). Unconstrained middleware (BH-MW) fell below its own prompt-only variant on Retail; the constraint, not the surface, is what makes middleware safely searchable.
- Route each failure to the right surface: prompts for global policy, middleware for locally-checkable execution invariants. Removing routing collapsed lift first-order on all three tasks; prompts alone miss runtime failures, unconstrained middleware adds selection risk.

Experiment setup (from the paper): fixed inner execution model gpt-5.4-mini, outer proposer claude-opus-4.7. Benchmarks: BFCL multi-round (600-case scorecard) and tau2-Retail / tau2-Telecom (74-case scorecard each of 114 tasks). Baselines BH, GEPA, MIPROv2 + PRISM; disjoint repair/gate/scorecard splits, 4 seeds, up to 16 runs. Baseline = native Deep Agents (v0.5.6). Metrics: mean held-out lift (pp), WorstLift, repeatability, RelLift95(B) by 5,000 bootstrap. PRISM-MW mean lifts 14.2 / 14.9 / 10.1 pp and positive RelLift95 on all three.
quotedTweet.translationZh:
Beyond Prompts: Measuring and Optimizing LLM Tool-Agent Harnesses —— 新论文（arXiv，2026 年 9 月 4 日；已被 EMNLP 2026 接收）。https://t.co/pKJEV3lx5R

将固定模型周围的 harness 优化视为有预算的选择问题：编辑是在工具边界设置的受控拦截，而不是重写执行逻辑。PRISM 会聚类失败，将每个修复路由到 prompt、中间件或联合表面，并按门控通过率和可靠性（RelLift95）选择候选，而不只看分数。

给产品构建者的 3 个明确启示：
- 报告所选 harness 的可靠性，而不只是平均提升。BH 找到了最佳的单个 harness，但在两个 tau-bench 领域的可靠提升为负，是强探索器，却是不可靠的选择器。
- 将中间件限制在工具边界编辑模式内（静默纠正、错误阻断、前置条件阻断）。不受约束的中间件（BH-MW）在 Retail 上低于其仅 prompt 版本；让中间件可被安全搜索的是约束，而不是表面本身。
- 将每个失败路由到正确表面：prompt 处理全局策略，中间件处理可在本地检查的执行不变量。移除路由后，三个任务的一阶提升都崩塌；仅靠 prompt 会遗漏运行时失败，不受约束的中间件会增加选择风险。

实验设置（来自论文）：固定内部执行模型 gpt-5.4-mini，外部提议器 claude-opus-4.7。基准：BFCL multi-round（600 个案例记分卡）和 tau2-Retail / tau2-Telecom（各 74 个案例记分卡，来自 114 个任务）。基线为 BH、GEPA、MIPROv2 + PRISM；修复/门控/记分卡拆分互不重叠，4 个种子，最多 16 次运行。Baseline = 原生 Deep Agents（v0.5.6）。指标：平均留出集提升（pp）、WorstLift、可重复性、通过 5,000 次 bootstrap 计算的 RelLift95(B)。PRISM-MW 的平均提升为 14.2 / 14.9 / 10.1 pp，并且在三项任务上 RelLift95 均为正。

posts.text:
Skill 搜到了，Agent 反而把原本会做的题做错了。

这篇《Skill Following》专门研究一个很容易会踩坑的问题。

现在评估 Agent Skill，通常会看「有 Skill」和「没 Skill」时整体分数差多少。

但这里有个偏差。Agent 往往只会在某些任务上主动检索 Skill，而这些任务本身可能就更简单或更适合检索。

作者因此提出 RAE，只看真正发生过 Skill 检索的任务，再对同一道题比较「用了 Skill」和「没用 Skill」的结果。

结果在 MBPP+ 上，DeepSeek-V3.2 按传统统计看，检索带来 +31.6 个百分点提升；换成 RAE 后却变成 -9.1。

Gemini-2.5-Flash-lite 也出现类似情况，+6.2 变成 -15.6。

这种现象在数学任务里同样存在。Llama-3.3-70B 在 Math500 上看起来提升 +14.2，真正的 RAE 却是 -39.4。

进一步分析发现，问题经常出在检索之后。

Agent 找到了 Skill，却没有真正用进去；有时理解错了，有时过度套用，还有时直接破坏了最终输出格式。

这篇给 Skill Agent 一个很重要的提醒。

「能检索到」和「能正确使用」其实是两种能力。

以后评估 Memory、Skill 或 RAG，也许都应该多问一句：这条外部知识被调用之后，究竟救回了多少任务，又弄坏了多少原本能做对的任务？

📎 arxiv: https://t.co/ZIMqhQJNY1

posts.text: Astra for medical education:

quotedTweet.text:
GPT-6 Astra just solved a problem medical students have been facing for decades

Medical students have been working around the same three problems for decades. Someone talked to them, identified all three, and built a service with Astra that solves them in one tool.

The problems are structural. Flat anatomical diagrams strip depth out of organs entirely. CT cross-sections don't connect naturally to the overview diagrams students spend years memorizing. And reading a scan requires holding three mental models simultaneously - patient orientation, cross-section direction, and how every organ shape shifts through each layer.

Astra built a service that handles all three in one place. Not a better textbook. A spatial tool that connects the diagram, the CT view, and the 3D relationship together.

Medical education hasn't changed its core format in over a century. This might be the first tool designed around how anatomy is actually understood - not just displayed.
quotedTweet.translationZh:
GPT-6 Astra 刚刚解决了医学生几十年来一直面对的问题

几十年来，医学生一直在绕开同样三个问题。有人与他们交流，识别出这三个问题，并用 Astra 构建了一个服务，在一个工具中解决了它们。

这些问题是结构性的。平面解剖图完全抹去了器官的深度。CT 横断面无法自然连接到学生多年记忆的总体示意图。读片还要求同时维持三套心智模型：患者方位、切面方向，以及每个器官形态如何在各层中变化。

Astra 构建了一个服务，把这三件事放在同一个地方处理。它不是一本更好的教材，而是一个空间工具，把示意图、CT 视图和 3D 关系连接起来。

医学教育的核心形式一个多世纪以来几乎没有改变。这可能是第一个围绕解剖学实际理解方式设计的工具，而不仅仅是展示解剖结构。

AI 能把蛋糕做得非常大，但蛋糕最后怎么分，是另一件事。

posts.text:
friends are regularly surprised when i say i don’t think math is (yet) “solved,” so in the wake of the ns result i figured i’d explain this take a bit more widely.

first, this is massively impressive and clearly an example of AI being, in some respects, far more powerful than the human mind. the team deserves huge praise for attempting and succeeding at this. i’d love to read a technical report on the project (one can always hope :)

but second, here again we ended up with a counterexample rather than a full proof: option C won the NS problem by proving the conjecture false (which was one valid way to solve the problem for sure)

notice a pattern in many of the recent frontier results in ai for math? a striking number involve counterexamples or finding a needle in a haystack.

now don’t get me wrong: this is extraordinarily hard and commendable. but it is only one aspect of mathematicians’ work.

Math is also about:
- finding deep, general mathematical understanding and explanations within proofs
- revisiting proven results to find more « elegant » proofs
- proposing new conjectures and hypotheses that might open « fruitful » directions
- taking the leap of faith of proposing entirely new, « exciting » research programs that may take decades to bear fruit

you may say these are simply further increments on the same intelligence scale, and perhaps point 2 above is already within the reach of current models. possibly

but you could also see this string of results as an extraordinarily powerful, massively parallel extension of search: explore the haystack, find the needle i.e. the counterexample that breaks the conjecture.

that would already be remarkable. but it would still leave open whether models understand the words I emphasized above: « elegant », « fruitful », « exciting ».

as tristan put it in his brief report: “the first llm generated proof levent sent me was the most horrendous i have ever read.”

despite their formidable technical abilities, models still seem to lack something mathematicians rely on constantly: a type of mathematical taste. the ability to distinguish a beautiful argument from a merely valid one, a fertile idea from a sterile one.

i’d be very curious to ask gpt or claude what they think of the result they just proved. do they find it elegant? if they ignore all the human noise about it on the web and history of math, do they appreciate the result and the path to it more than other proofs?

my suspicion is that, outside of the human knowledge that this is an important millennium prize problem, it may not 100% register it as fundamentally different from thousands of other proofs.

or, more intriguingly, perhaps the beauty they find in mathematics is actually alien to our own sense of mathematical beauty, some « horrendous » proof to us might be deeply satisfying to them…

all this to say that we might have significant progress to make in ai for math before declaring the field “solved,” (as too many are posting).

in the meantime, ai will be an extraordinary collaborator for mathematicians. i just hope access to these tools be as widely shared as possible (so that you don’t need a Leven or Sebastien working in a big lab to help you), and that companies stop using mathematics primarily as a demonstration of prowess in their private race.

editorial.rationale: 含AI数学事实但证据不足

posts.translationZh:
朋友们经常会惊讶于我说我认为数学（目前）还没有被“解决”，所以在 ns 结果之后，我想更广泛地解释一下这个看法。

首先，这非常令人震撼，显然也说明 AI 在某些方面远比人类头脑强大。这个团队敢于尝试并取得成功，值得高度赞扬。我很想读一份关于这个项目的技术报告（总还是可以期待一下 :）

但其次，我们这次又一次得到的是一个反例，而不是完整证明：选项 C 通过证明猜想为假赢下了 NS 问题（这当然也是解决该问题的一种有效方式）。

注意到近期 AI 数学前沿成果中的一个模式了吗？相当多都涉及反例，或者是在大海捞针中找到那根针。

别误会：这极其困难，也非常值得赞赏。但这只是数学家工作的一部分。

数学还包括：
- 在证明中找到深刻、普遍的数学理解和解释
- 重新审视已被证明的结果，寻找更“优雅”的证明
- 提出可能开启“富有成效”方向的新猜想和假设
- 凭信念跃迁，提出全新的、“令人兴奋”的研究计划，而这些计划可能需要数十年才会结果

你可能会说，这些只是同一智能尺度上的进一步增量，也许上面的第 2 点已经在当前模型的能力范围内。或许如此。

但你也可以把这一系列结果看作是搜索能力的极其强大、超大规模并行扩展：探索草垛，找到那根针，也就是击破猜想的反例。

这本身已经很了不起。但问题仍然存在：模型是否理解我上面强调的那些词：“优雅”、“富有成效”、“令人兴奋”。

正如 tristan 在他的简短报告中所说：“levent 发给我的第一个 llm 生成证明，是我读过的最可怕的证明。”

尽管模型具备强大的技术能力，它们似乎仍然缺少数学家一直依赖的一种东西：数学品味。也就是区分美的论证和仅仅有效的论证、区分有生命力的想法和贫瘠想法的能力。

我很想问问 gpt 或 claude，它们如何看待自己刚刚证明的结果。它们觉得这个结果优雅吗？如果忽略网上的人类噪音和数学史，它们是否会比其他证明更欣赏这个结果以及通往它的路径？

我的怀疑是，如果脱离“这是一个重要的千禧年大奖难题”这一人类知识，它可能并不会 100% 意识到它与成千上万其他证明有根本不同。

或者更有意思的是，也许它们在数学中发现的美，其实与我们自己的数学美感完全不同；某个对我们来说“可怕”的证明，对它们来说或许会非常令人满足……

总之，我想说的是，在宣布数学 AI 领域已被“解决”（现在太多人这样发帖了）之前，我们可能还有相当多进展要做。

与此同时，AI 会成为数学家的非凡合作者。我只是希望这些工具能尽可能广泛地共享（这样你不需要有在大实验室工作的 Leven 或 Sebastien 来帮你），也希望公司不要主要把数学当作它们私下竞赛中展示实力的工具。

"Discovery consists of seeing what everybody has seen, and thinking what nobody has thought."
(Albert Szent-Györgyi)

quotedTweet.text:
What we’re witnessing right now in AI for math is a dramatic improvement in objective-driven problem-solving, but it does not speak to non-objective discovery. I have always maintained that objectives are achievable when they are one stepping stone away, which means that they are within reach if their necessary prerequisite stepping stones are already laid. We say as much in Why Greatness Cannot Be Planned.

Furthermore, I have identified “the stepping stepping already laid” as every invention and idea ever hatched over the course of human history.  That is the frontier of civilization.  But a massive challenge for every creative field is to make all the relevant stepping stones actually accessible to its practitioners.  How can anyone be aware of all of human knowledge in their field? To the extent they cannot, some dots cannot be connected even if they’re already uncovered.

AI advances today have suddenly made the existing stepping stones vastly more accessible.  It can see something close to “all” of them, which means it has the possibility of leaping to many more next stepping stones in the chain.  Combined with a brute force-ish “try every known stepping stone under the sun”, that’s what we’re seeing in the pursuit of popular objectives.

But discovery and innovation are not only about finding the right existing stepping stones to solve your objective because for many problems the stepping stones are not already laid and also do not follow directly from existing stepping stones. If those problems are ever to be solved, they will require open-ended, non-objective search through spaces of ideas that are motivated not by solving a problem as an objective, but by being interesting in their own right.  The advances we’re seeing today speak only faintly to that purpose, which is why open-endedness remains firmly at the frontier of AI.
quotedTweet.translationZh:
我们现在在 AI 数学领域看到的，是目标驱动型问题求解能力的大幅提升，但这并不代表非目标导向的发现能力也在进步。我一直认为，当目标只隔着一块垫脚石时，它就是可达成的，也就是说，只要必要的前置垫脚石已经铺好，它就触手可及。我们在《Why Greatness Cannot Be Planned》中也表达过类似观点。

此外，我把“已经铺好的垫脚石”定义为人类历史进程中曾经诞生过的每一项发明和每一个想法。这就是文明的前沿。但对每个创造性领域来说，一个巨大挑战是如何让从业者真正接触到所有相关的垫脚石。谁能知晓自己领域内的全部人类知识？只要做不到这一点，有些点即便已经被发现，也仍然无法连接起来。

如今的 AI 进展突然让现有垫脚石变得极大程度上更易获取。它几乎能看到“全部”垫脚石，这意味着它有可能跳到链条中更多的下一块垫脚石。再结合某种近似蛮力的“尝试天下所有已知垫脚石”的方法，这就是我们在追求热门目标时所看到的现象。

但发现和创新并不只是找到正确的现有垫脚石来解决你的目标，因为对许多问题来说，垫脚石尚未铺好，也不会直接从现有垫脚石中推导出来。如果这些问题终有一天要被解决，就需要在思想空间中进行开放式、非目标导向的搜索，其动机不是把解决某个问题当作目标，而是这些想法本身就足够有趣。我们今天看到的进展对这一目的只有很微弱的启示，因此开放性仍然稳稳处在 AI 的前沿。

friends are regularly surprised when i say i don’t think math is (yet) “solved,” so in the wake of the ns result i figured i’d explain this take a bit more widely.

first, this is massively impressive and clearly an example of AI being, in some respects, far more powerful than the human mind. the team deserves huge praise for attempting and succeeding at this. i’d love to read a technical report on the project (one can always hope :)

but second, here again we ended up with a counterexample rather than a full proof: option C won the NS problem by proving the conjecture false (which was one valid way to solve the problem for sure)

notice a pattern in many of the recent frontier results in ai for math? a striking number involve counterexamples or finding a needle in a haystack.

now don’t get me wrong: this is extraordinarily hard and commendable. but it is only one aspect of mathematicians’ work.

Math is also about:
- finding deep, general mathematical understanding and explanations within proofs
- revisiting proven results to find more « elegant » proofs
- proposing new conjectures and hypotheses that might open « fruitful » directions
- taking the leap of faith of proposing entirely new, « exciting » research programs that may take decades to bear fruit

you may say these are simply further increments on the same intelligence scale, and perhaps point 2 above is already within the reach of current models. possibly

but you could also see this string of results as an extraordinarily powerful, massively parallel extension of search: explore the haystack, find the needle i.e. the counterexample that breaks the conjecture.

that would already be remarkable. but it would still leave open whether models understand the words I emphasized above: « elegant », « fruitful », « exciting ».

as tristan put it in his brief report: “the first llm generated proof levent sent me was the most horrendous i have ever read.”

despite their formidable technical abilities, models still seem to lack something mathematicians rely on constantly: a type of mathematical taste. the ability to distinguish a beautiful argument from a merely valid one, a fertile idea from a sterile one.

i’d be very curious to ask gpt or claude what they think of the result they just proved. do they find it elegant? if they ignore all the human noise about it on the web and history of math, do they appreciate the result and the path to it more than other proofs?

my suspicion is that, outside of the human knowledge that this is an important millennium prize problem, it may not 100% register it as fundamentally different from thousands of other proofs.

or, more intriguingly, perhaps the beauty they find in mathematics is actually alien to our own sense of mathematical beauty, some « horrendous » proof to us might be deeply satisfying to them…

all this to say that we might have significant progress to make in ai for math before declaring the field “solved,” (as too many are posting).

in the meantime, ai will be an extraordinary collaborator for mathematicians. i just hope access to these tools be as widely shared as possible (so that you don’t need a Leven or Sebastien working in a big lab to help you), and that companies stop using mathematics primarily as a demonstration of prowess in their private race.

那些真正值得保留的，是那些 AI 最难替你决定的东西，例如为什么写这一段、为什么选这个例子、什么该删、你到底观察到了什么，以及你希望读者看完以后留下什么。

我现在觉得，AI 时代做内容，一个很重要的能力可能就是提高自己的 Intent Density「意图密度」。

AI 可以帮你把东西做出来，但最后那层「为什么这样做」，还是得自己放进去。

Skill 搜到了，Agent 反而把原本会做的题做错了。

这篇《Skill Following》专门研究一个很容易会踩坑的问题。

现在评估 Agent Skill，通常会看「有 Skill」和「没 Skill」时整体分数差多少。

但这里有个偏差。Agent 往往只会在某些任务上主动检索 Skill，而这些任务本身可能就更简单或更适合检索。

作者因此提出 RAE，只看真正发生过 Skill 检索的任务，再对同一道题比较「用了 Skill」和「没用 Skill」的结果。

结果在 MBPP+ 上，DeepSeek-V3.2 按传统统计看，检索带来 +31.6 个百分点提升；换成 RAE 后却变成 -9.1。

Gemini-2.5-Flash-lite 也出现类似情况，+6.2 变成 -15.6。

这种现象在数学任务里同样存在。Llama-3.3-70B 在 Math500 上看起来提升 +14.2，真正的 RAE 却是 -39.4。

进一步分析发现，问题经常出在检索之后。

Agent 找到了 Skill，却没有真正用进去；有时理解错了，有时过度套用，还有时直接破坏了最终输出格式。

这篇给 Skill Agent 一个很重要的提醒。

「能检索到」和「能正确使用」其实是两种能力。

以后评估 Memory、Skill 或 RAG，也许都应该多问一句：这条外部知识被调用之后，究竟救回了多少任务，又弄坏了多少原本能做对的任务？

📎 arxiv: https://t.co/ZIMqhQJNY1

Hi Jack, nice work! One thing I've been thinking about for months and didn't see addressed here (curious what you think) is the consumption side.

In the model, whatever is produced is assumed to be bought. But if the labor share falls and the gains go to capital, who is spending? The caveats mention demand effects and the conclusion leaves it to redistribution later. Is this not this what decides whether the growth happens at all?

It also seems different from previous revolutions, where the new goods eventually showed up in household budgets: cars, appliances, phones. Cognitive output is mostly an input to work, not something households buy for living or leisure. You might point to health care as the sector with unmet demand, but how do people pay for advanced therapeutics if the income that would buy them has just moved to capital? I do not see how you can close the loop without that consumption.
